messages:
Nina: uploaded a compact onboarding banner variant — bottom-left floating card (doesn't push nav). Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/efgh/onboard-compact. Thoughts on visibility + screen reader behavior?
Jonah: love less vertical real estate use. Concern: if it's bottom-left it might overlap terminal/log panels. We should hide it on very small height breakpoints (<640px). :warning:
Priya: accessibility nits: need clear heading semantics and ensure banner is in DOM order before main for SR users, but visually placed bottom-left via CSS. Add aria-describedby to CTA for extra context.
Nina: agreed. Plan: DOM-first, visual position via transform. No autofocus. Add role="dialog"? maybe role="region" to avoid modal semantics.
UX Bot: checklist: non-modal region, aria-live polite for state changes, visible focus styles, contrast ratio >=4.5 for body text. Also callout: ensure close button has accessible name (aria-label="Dismiss onboarding").
Jonah: analytics: event=onboard_compact_shown, action=complete_setup, action=try_sample_project, dismiss_reason values (close, already_setup, not_now).
Priya: copy tweak suggestion: primary CTA "Finish setup" (short), secondary "Explore sample project". Add microcopy under CTA: "Recommended for first-time users" — ensure contrast.
Nina: I'll update figma and open a small PR with CSS approach + aria attributes. PR link will be in thread when ready. Also will add a keyboard shortcut to reopen the helper (Shift+Alt+O) and show in Help menu.
Dev Tools Bot: created issue #792: implement compact onboarding banner. Assigning to @Nina.
Jonah: quick usability idea — add a subtle pulsing dot on the Help icon if user dismisses without finishing, to nudge re-open. Must be testable and optional via feature flag.
Priya: +1 on flag. Also let's run a 5-person hallway test focused on discoverability. I'll schedule for next Tue.
Nina: thanks team. Follow-ups: 1) PR with DOM-first + CSS placement, 2) fix subtitle contrast, 3) add telemetry keys, 4) Help reopen shortcut. Will post updates here. :thumbsup:
